old_title: Nepal-Tibet floods live: Death toll passes 580, nearly 2,500 people missing
new_title: Rescuers search for hundreds still missing in Nepal-Tibet disaster area as death toll climbs
old_text:
Nepal-Tibet floods live: Death toll passes 580, nearly 2,500 people missing
Rescuers in Tibet reached the main area wiped out by a devastating mudslide this week, Chinese state media reported, as the search for missing people battled treacherous conditions. The devastating flooding in Nepal and Tibet has claimed more than 580 lives and left some 2,500 missing. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
• The search for 1,300 people continued after landslides caused by a glacial collapse unleashed a torrent of mud and water across Nepal and China's autonomous region of Tibet.
• Nepal and China both warned of fresh risks of flooding in the Himalayas as two lakes that have developed on either side of their border threaten to burst.
• Devastating floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have killed at least 359 people, Nepali police said in an update.
(FRANCE 24 with Reuters, AP and AFP)
new_text:
Rescuers search for hundreds still missing in Nepal-Tibet disaster area as death toll climbs
Rescuers in Tibet reached the main area wiped out by a devastating mudslide this week, Chinese state media reported, as the search for missing people battled treacherous conditions. The devastating flooding in Nepal and Tibet has claimed more than 580 lives and left more than 2,400 missing. Read our live blog to see how all the day's events unfolded.
Thank you for following this live blog
The number of people missing in Nepal and China has surpassed 2,400, underscoring the scale of the disaster days after a tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept away villages and killed hundreds.
Click on the link below for the full story.
🎥 Families cling to hope amid frantic search for survivors
Families continue to search hospitals and disaster zones in the hope their loved ones will be found alive, with nearly 2,500 people still missing.
More than 3,700 people have been rescued so far, though destroyed roads, bridges and thick mud continue to hamper search efforts.
Mother reunited with 8-year-old who climbed trees to survive floods
Zoyal Ghale, who ran into a forest and climbed trees to escape Nepal's deadly floods, was reunited with his mother earlier today after she had begun to fear he and his brother had both perished in their school.
A day earlier, 8-year-old Ghale had been airlifted alone from the devastated northern district of Rasuwa with a broken leg and cuts on his face, while his mother, Matti Maya Tamang, 28, moved from one shelter and collection point to another looking for her two missing children.
Zoyal Ghale, 8, speaks with his mother inside a hospital in Kathmandu. Credit: Ranup Shrestha, Reuters
"At the fourth place too, my children's names were not on the list, and they were not there," Tamang told Reuters. "I had come to accept that both my children were no more. All I could do was weep. I couldn't hold myself together at all."
She had already found her younger son alive as well.
Canada announces CAN$5 million in aid after Nepal flood
Canada will provide CAN$5 million (US$ 3.6 million) in funding to help relief operations in Nepal, the government has said.
"We are announcing that Canada is providing $5 million in humanitarian assistance to support emergency relief efforts in Nepal," Randeep Sarai, Canada's secretary of state for international development, told reporters.
🎥 'Region has hundreds of high-altitude lakes prone to unleashing enormous volumes of water'
We speak to David Fisher, head of the International Federation of the Red Cross for Nepal, about the scale of the disaster, the huge challenges faced by rescue workers, and the risk of further flooding from upstream lakes.
Four French nationals missing, foreign ministry confirms
Four French nationals are missing following the devastating floods in Nepal and China, the French Foreign Ministry has said, confirming a figure given the previous day by the Nepalese authorities.
"The French Embassy in Kathmandu is liaising with the local authorities in an attempt to locate them. Teams from the Crisis and Support Centre are in contact with the families of our nationals," added the ministry's deputy spokesperson, Glenn Salic.
Number of missing people soars to nearly 2,500
The number of people missing in Nepal and China has leapt to nearly 2,500, including close to 2,000 in Nepal alone, underscoring the scale of the disaster.
Rescuers are battling through mud even as the threat of new floods looms, with emergency teams recovering 584 bodies so far -- and some of the dead swept downstream as far away as India.
The new figures come as Nepal's disaster authority added 933 hydropower workers to a missing list already including trekkers and pilgrims to Tibet's sacred Mount Kailash.
UN agency warns of 17,000 children in urgent need of assistance
The UN's agency for children says at least 17,000 children are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance.
UNICEF says 18 schools have been destroyed and another 20 damaged, with remaining facilities turned into emergency shelters.
📸 In pictures: Scenes of devastation and a harrowing search for the missing
A man walks past damaged structures after flash flooding in the Devighat area of Nuwakot district in Nepal. Credit: Rajesh Kumar Singh, AP
Residents salvage their belongings from damaged houses after flash flooding in the Devighat area. Credit: Rajesh Kumar Singh, AP
People look at photographs of people killed in the flash floods displayed outside a government hospital in Kathmandu, Nepal. Credit: Dar Yasin, AP
Nepal death toll rises to 579, nearly 2,000 people missing
Nepal's disaster management authority says the death toll has risen to 579.
The agency said the number of people reported missing has doubled to 1,924, as more local residents were added to the tally.
The number of foreign nationals reported missing remains at 517.
Rescuers grapple with mountain of challenges after the Nepal-Tibet floods
Emergency services are rushing to find survivors and treat the wounded after a devastating flash flood on the border of Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday killed more than 500 people, with over a thousand still missing.
But the remote and rugged terrain, as well as the risk of further flooding from upstream lakes formed by piles of debris, make their work as delicate as it is dangerous.
EU pledges two million euros in Nepal flood aid
The European Union has promised two million euros ($2.3 mn) in aid for Nepal following the devastating flash floods.
European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen wrote on X that the "immediate humanitarian aid" would help "deliver life-saving assistance to families and communities hit hardest".
'Ran for our lives': Survivors recount terrifying escape
Some survivors of the deadly floods on the Nepal-China border ran for their lives, others narrowly missed disaster, but all were eyewitnesses to a major calamity and its aftermath.
Sivaranjani Muthunathan was travelling by bus with 56 others from India's southern state of Tamil Nadu when they became stuck in what they thought was a traffic jam.
"Then there was fog, smoke, something that seemed to suddenly engulf us," she told AFP, showing a video she recorded on her phone of a torrent surging towards her.
Vehicles were swept away or buried under mud around them.
"One by one, we climbed out through the driver's side," she said. "Every vehicle in front of us, behind us, was gone."
Click on the link below for the full story.
Nepal floods explained: The chain of events behind the disaster
A glacier broke apart. An ice and rock avalanche followed. Then came an earthquake, before a landslide triggered devastating floods that tore through kilometres of valley.
This is what happened along the Nepal-China border, where rescue teams are still trying to recover survivors 48 hours after the catastrophe.
This video breaks down the chain of events and offers the scientific explanations behind the disaster.
Nepal declines foreign rescue help, South Korea says it is 'negotiating'
Nepal does not need foreign assistance for search-and-rescue operations, its foreign ministry has said, despite offers of help from several countries with nationals missing in the disaster.
Hundreds of foreign nationals are still missing, including from South Korea, which said it has already sent a response team to Nepal and will also dispatch a disaster relief team.
"The offer for help is natural. Our security agencies are doing the search and rescue operation. For now we don't require such help," Lok Bahadur Chhetri, spokesperson for Nepal's foreign ministry, said without providing further details.
The Kathmandu Post reported that India, China, the United States, Britain, Japan, South Korea, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh had asked the government to allow their search-and-rescue teams to assist in the operation.
South Korea's foreign ministry said Nepal had indicated it was not yet planning to accept foreign rescue teams.
"South Korea will keep negotiating with Nepal over the matter," the ministry added.
📸 In pictures: Families look for missing people in Nepal
Lists of missing persons, accompanied by photographs, are posted on the streets of Kathmandu. © AFP
A relative consoles Jenisha, centre, as she cries while waiting for the news of her father missing after flash flooding in Nepal's Nuwakot district, on August 28, 2026. © Rajesh Kumar Singh, AP
🎥 Army rescues hundreds trapped in hydropower tunnel
🎥 Around 93,000 people affected, according to the Red Cross
The death toll continues to rise in the Nepal and Tibet floods as the situation remains fast-moving.
The Red Cross says around 93,000 people have been affected. International aid is arriving from several countries, but rescue efforts have been hampered by the difficulty of coordinating operations in the remote Himalayan terrain.
The epicentre of the disaster was only reached 48 hours after the floods began.
FRANCE 24's Jamie Smith-Maillet has the latest.
Nepal floods trauma 'enormous', Red Cross says
The level of trauma cascading from the Nepal flash floods is "enormous", the Red Cross said, with early estimates suggesting 93,000 people may have been affected.
The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), the world's largest humanitarian network, fears the death toll from Wednesday's disaster, already above 500, will continue to rise.
"Due to roads and bridges having been washed out and both cell coverage and electricity cuts, we have not yet been able to access some of the hardest-hit areas," said David Fisher, the IFRC head of delegation for Nepal.
"The trauma of this event is enormous," he told a press conference in Geneva, speaking from Kathmandu.
• The search for 1,300 people continued after landslides caused by a glacial collapse unleashed a torrent of mud and water across Nepal and China's autonomous region of Tibet.
• Nepal and China both warned of fresh risks of flooding in the Himalayas as two lakes that have developed on either side of their border threaten to burst.
• Devastating floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have killed at least 359 people, Nepali police said in an update.
(FRANCE 24 with Reuters, AP and AFP)
